clue.text: Whip swears ditching regulars is more sensible  …

indicators.note: throwing away the letters at regular intervals leaves only every other one of the phrase

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters are kept

explanation.surface: A party whip who stops swearing at backbenchers is showing better judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip is the party official who keeps MPs voting in line. The ellipsis joins this clue to the next one in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiser is the comparative of wise, describing someone showing better judgement or good sense.

clue.text: Changing seawater left government looking after everyone

indicators.note: changing the letters around means they are set in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rising sea levels have left the authorities with a duty to protect the whole population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction or a political wing, but every letter of it goes into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A welfare state is a system in which the government provides health care, pensions and benefits for all citizens.

clue.text: Tune that can make a singer's name

blocks.clueFragment: Tune that can make a singer's name
blocks.note: surface reading: a hit song that makes a performer famous
setter's reading: the word that comes before tune in the phrase for a performer's trademark song, and also an autograph

explanation.walkthrough: A performer's trademark song is their 'signature tune'; the first word alone means a written name, so 'tune' leads to the phrase while 'name' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature is a person's name written in their own hand, as a singer signs an autograph.

clue.text: Turner too rough to sit in a posh car?

indicators.note: roughed up, the letters are knocked out of their original order
sitting in a vehicle puts one thing inside another

blocks.note: RR is a Rolls-Royce, the classic posh car
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the painter Turner too scruffy to ride in a luxury limousine?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter J. M. W. Turner; it is simply something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine such as a helicopter or motor, literally a thing that turns.

clue.text: …  but leaving one out of picnic is not so bright

definitions.text: but leaving one out of picnic is not so bright

blocks.note: surface reading: someone forgets an item from the hamper on an outing
setter's reading: the idiom about being one item short of a picnic, meaning rather dim

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: forgetting something for the picnic is not the cleverest move.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'one sandwich short of a picnic' means not very intelligent; take one away and the picnic is incomplete, like the person's wits.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the missing picnic item from the idiom used to call someone a little slow-witted.

clue.text: Getting even for second low affair

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
to low is to make the noise a cow makes
a thing is an informal word for a romance or affair

explanation.surface: Taking revenge on a partner by having a second shabby fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting even' suggests revenge, but it means making a surface level; 'low' is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoothing a surface removes bumps, making it flat and level, which is literally getting it even.

clue.text: King left ring at funeral for his theatrical mistress

indicators.note: left here means departed, so the royal letter goes away

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a knell is the bell tolled for a death

explanation.surface: A king leaves the church as bells toll for the death of his actress lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn was an actress and the mistress of King Charles II, so 'his' refers back to the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Nell Gwyn, the Restoration actress, was the famous lover of Charles II of England.

clue.text: About time wage rate changes create a scandal

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged words go round the abbreviation
the letters change places, giving a new arrangement

blocks.note: the two words' letters, rearranged
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Changing pay levels at last stirs up a public outcry.
explanation.walkthrough: Watergate was the 1970s US political scandal that brought down President Nixon.
explanation.definitionFit: The break-in and cover-up of the 1970s became the archetypal political scandal in America.

clue.text: Singers introducing common Handel oratorio in recital

indicators.note: words that introduce something stand at its start, so the leading letters are taken

blocks.note: initial letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A group of vocalists opens a concert with a familiar Handel piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised group of people who sing together, often in churches or concerts.

clue.text: Stars won't be seen in this humorous rubbish

definitions.text: Stars won't be seen in this

blocks.note: light verse or light entertainment is humorous
rubbish dumped in the environment fouls it

explanation.surface: A dismissive critic says a comedy is so bad no film stars would appear in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The stars are celestial, not celebrities: glare from city lamps hides them.
explanation.definitionFit: Artificial brightness from towns washes out the night sky, so most celestial bodies become invisible to observers.

clue.text: Challenge test results showing evidence of skin damage

blocks.note: a task that stretches you is a challenge
marks are the scores given in an exam

explanation.surface: Results from a tough dermatology test reveal harm to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: These streaky scars appear where skin has been overstretched, for example after pregnancy or rapid growth.

clue.text: Eagerness of first-rate amateurs to take credit

indicators.note: the amateurs take in the credit, holding it inside their own word

blocks.note: A is the top grade, as in A1
the laity are people outside a profession
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Top amateur players eagerly claim the glory for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: A is the top grade, as in A1; CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit, and it lands inside the word for non-professionals.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity is brisk readiness or keenness to do something, a close synonym for eagerness.

clue.text: Doctor turning Conservative might bring the house down

indicators.note: turning round means the party member's word is read from its last letter back

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for doctor
Tory is the everyday name for a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A doctor defecting to the Conservatives could cause uproar in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring the house down' suggests applause or Parliament; here it is literal, a building collapsing from fungal decay.
explanation.definitionFit: This timber fungus weakens beams and floors so badly that a building can eventually collapse.

clue.text: Knowledge of game put into publication

indicators.note: one item is placed inside another, so the game sits within the publication

blocks.note: an edition is one issue of a published work
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Expertise on a sport finds its way into a book.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) is a common crossword game.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep learning acquired through study, a scholarly kind of knowledge.

clue.text: Popular English stage setter loses nothing being crude

indicators.note: nothing is a zero, the round letter, and losing it drops that letter

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
standard abbreviation
a leg is one stage of a journey or race
the pseudonym of the person who compiled this puzzle

explanation.surface: A popular English stage designer's work turns out to be vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage setter' reads as a theatre designer; split it, and 'setter' is the puzzle's compiler, Anto, who loses an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude can mean lacking refinement or grace, which is what inelegant describes.

clue.text: Newcomers one prepared with scraps picked up

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up, so the letters are made into a fresh order
picked up as in heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the three letters of one, rearranged
scraps are fights or brawls

explanation.surface: A newcomer readies themselves with leftover bits of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraps' suggests leftovers, but it means fights, and the sound is spelt PHYTES.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophytes are beginners or novices, people new to a subject, religion or activity.

clue.text: It can be painful or pleasing, if well turned

definitions.text: It can be painful or pleasing, if well turned

blocks.note: surface reading: something that hurts, such as a joint twisted badly
setter's reading: a well-turned one is a shapely lower leg admired in old novels

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' works twice: a joint turned over in a sprain hurts, while 'well-turned' is a compliment on elegant shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This joint above the foot hurts when sprained, and a slender, well-shaped one was once praised as attractive.

clue.text: A worker upset about an eastern conflict

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into another order
about means around, so the jumbled letters enclose the short word

blocks.note: the letters of both words, jumbled
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unhappy labourer grumbles about a war in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The Korean War of 1950 to 1953 was fought in East Asia between North and South Korea and their allies.

clue.text: Subject of article on chronic fatigue condition

blocks.note: the definite article
ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, is chronic fatigue syndrome

explanation.surface: The topic of a magazine piece about chronic fatigue.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the main topic or idea that a talk, essay or work concerns.

clue.text: Design style even squares will be seen in

definitions.text: Design style even squares will be seen in

blocks.note: surface reading: squares as dull, conventional people, who even they might wear
setter's reading: a pattern built from regular shapes, where squares naturally appear

explanation.surface: A fashion so mainstream that even the most conventional people would be seen in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squares' tempts you to think of unfashionable people; it means the shape, at home in a pattern of lines, circles and polygons.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric design uses regular shapes such as squares, triangles and circles arranged in a pattern.

clue.text: Medication found back in hotel bathroom

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
back tells you to read the concealed letters from right to left

blocks.note: concealed across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Pills left behind in a hotel bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a pill, a small solid dose of medicine taken by mouth.

clue.text: Stick with extremely clannish set

indicators.note: at the extremes means the very ends, so just the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: a bat is a club or stick used in games
first and last letters only

explanation.surface: Stay loyal to an exclusive, close-knit group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick with' reads as a phrasal verb; 'Stick' is the noun and 'with' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch is a group or set of things produced or handled together.

clue.text: Vision of man's path being troubled

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and unsettled, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A ghostly apparition appears on a troubled man's road.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantasm is an illusion or apparition, something seen that is not really there.

clue.text: Warrior sheltered by woman in jail

indicators.note: sheltered means kept inside, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A fighter is protected by a woman who is in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a covert Japanese warrior trained in stealth and martial arts.

clue.text: Go off search engine displaying dirty look

definitions.note: the answer here is the noun, a leering glance

indicators.note: off means removed, so the first word is taken away from the second

blocks.note: taken as written
the best-known web search engine

explanation.surface: Someone quits browsing the web after finding something smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogle is a leering or lecherous stare, the kind of look described as dirty.

clue.text: Surprisingly open response to a cryptic clue, perhaps

definitions.text: Surprisingly open response to a cryptic clue, perhaps

blocks.note: surface reading: a frank, honest reply where you expected evasion
setter's reading: what solvers get when a puzzle's riddle has a plain, untwisted solution

explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' looks like an anagram signal; it is not. The joke is that a cryptic clue rarely has a plain solution.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a frank, honest reply, and literally a solution that involves no twist.

clue.text: Distributing the last hundred items of personal property  …

indicators.note: handing things out spreads them around, so the letters are dealt into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: An executor hands out the final hundred possessions of an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Chattels are movable possessions, belongings a person owns other than land or buildings.

clue.text: …  landed estates, as housing credit halved

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun for areas of land

indicators.note: cut in two, so only the front portion of that word remains
a house holds things inside it, so the short word wraps round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the first three of its six letters

explanation.surface: Continuing the will: the country properties are mortgaged after the credit was cut in half.
explanation.definitionFit: Acres are units of land area, used loosely for broad estates or lands owned.
